ruling_verdicts.ruling: S2-operator-channel-recurrence-r12 (P2) — acceptance criterion per kimi arbitration ruling-set block: '(a) every operator-owned claim regardless of status appears in blocking_claims or a known_limits entry naming it (owner field present), or (b) a recorded operator ruling ... with the criterion's letter amended in the same artifact so the register and the derivation agree'; falsifier threshold: 'Zero unlisted operator-owned claims, or the ruling artifact exists and the amended criterion text matches the derivation.'
ruling_verdicts.basis: MET on the threshold's second disjunct, with every non-channeled claim covered by the ruling's own limbs. (i) OPERATOR RULING EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED: .ledger/entries.jsonl line 18, id v6-s2-operator-channel-law-20260818-18, present in C's tree (git show 16b80ac:.ledger/entries.jsonl grep count = 1). It rules a hybrid STRONGER than the criterion's (b) letter: LIMITED P1/P2 operator claims MUST occupy the known_limits machine channel via generator-DERIVED entries (claim field), non-PROVED non-LIMITED P1/P2 stay in blocking_claims via derive_blocking, PROVED are row-only, P3 census rows channel via the reconciliation artifact per acceptance-procedure item 3 — i.e., machine-channel-DERIVED, not an exemption; it answers exactly the question the arbitration's Next-action item 2 posed. (ii) CHANNEL CLASSIFICATION AT C+1 (7ce03b9, working tree verified clean, 0 dirty): 72 matrix claims, 7 with 'operator' in owner, each channeled per the law — CLM-RELEASE-AUTH (PROVED/P1/operator) row-only; CLM-MERGE-190, CLM-MERGE-156, CLM-MERGE-192 (PROVED/P1/operator) row-only; CLM-DESCRIPTION-BUDGET (LIMITED/P2/operator, the S2 defect claim) named by known_limits entry KL-OPERATOR-DESCRIPTION-BUDGET via its claim field, owner field present ('operator'), kind operator-hold, statement/release_consequence byte-consistent with the generator derivation; CLM-ISSUE-186 (PARTIAL/P3/operator+agent) census row = reconciliation item (issue,186), disposition decided-disarm-as-authorization, owner operator+agent, evidence_note D6; CLM-ISSUE-40 (PARTIAL/P3/operator) census row = reconciliation item (issue,40), disposition decided-rescope, owner operator, evidence_note D9. Zero operator-owned claims outside their lawful channel; blocking_claims == ['CLM-INDEPENDENT-GAUNTLET'] (owner independent-panel, UNPROVED P1 — correctly derived). Cross-checks: 46 census claims align 1:1 with 46 reconciliation items, zero owner mismatches, zero orphans in either direction; only recon items with operator-owner are issues 40 and 186; distinct owner strings in matrix are exactly {agent, independent-panel, joint, operator, operator+agent, program} so the case-sensitive substring test is exhaustive. (iii) REGISTER TEXT AGREES WITH DERIVATION CODE. Register (requirement-register.json, top-level operator_channel_law): authority = 'Operator ruling 2026-08-18 (S2, run es-v6-rc2-gauntlet-kimi-2026-08-18, CL-2 synthesis); amends the R12 criterion's letter so register and derivation agree per that ruling's path (b) mechanism'; law[0] = 'Every P1/P2 claim whose owner contains \'operator\' occupies a machine channel while open: blocking_claims for non-PROVED non-LIMITED statuses (derive_blocking), or a known_limits entry naming it via its `claim` field for LIMITED (derived by the generator, operator_limited_limits).'; law[1] = 'PROVED operator-owned claims are completed acts and are row-only.'; law[2] = 'P3 tracker census rows are channeled by the reconciliation artifact and walked at acceptance-procedure item 3, not duplicated into known_limits.'; enforced_by = 'validate_v6_assurance.validate_operator_channel (fails closed on any drop)'. Generator (.github/scripts/v6_generate_candidate_packet.py:1019-1046 operator_limited_limits): predicate '"operator" in claim["owner"] and claim["status"] == "LIMITED" and claim.get("consequence_severity") in ("P1", "P2")' -> derives {id: KL-OPERATOR-<claim-suffix>, kind: operator-hold, claim: <claim id>, statement, release_consequence, owner}; appended to known_limits at :1217; blocking_from_matrix (:1008-1016) imports derive_blocking from the validator (one home). Validator (plugins/epistemic-skills/contracts/v6-assurance/validate_v6_assurance.py:333-366 validate_operator_channel): skips non-operator owners, skips severity P3, skips PROVED, else requires claim id in blocking_claims OR in known_limits claim-field names, raising 'S2 CHANNEL DROP: operator-owned {status} claim {cid} appears in neither blocking_claims nor a known_limits entry naming it (claim field)'; derive_blocking (:58-75) blocks 'owner in OPERATOR_CLASS_OWNERS and status not in {PROVED, LIMITED} and severity != P3' (OPERATOR_CLASS_OWNERS = {operator, operator+agent, joint, independent-panel}, :45); validate_blocking_derivation (:319-330) pins packet blocking_claims == derive_blocking exactly, so the per-status channel assignment cannot be hand-shuffled; both wired in main() at :454-455. JUDGMENT: the register text and the derivation agree limb-for-limb — LIMITED P1/P2 -> operator_limited_limits derivation matches law[0]'s second arm; non-PROVED non-LIMITED P1/P2 operator-owned -> derive_blocking's third arm matches law[0]'s first arm (derive_blocking is additionally broader for joint/independent-panel/BLOCKED/P1-any-owner, which the law does not forbid); PROVED skip matches law[1]; P3 skip + reconciliation/procedure-item-3 routing matches law[2] (procedure item 3 names D9/#40 and D6/#186 explicitly). Wording 'owner contains operator' matches the code's substring test verbatim. (iv) TESTS AT C+1 in a fresh scratch clone (git clone --no-local, checked out 7ce03b9, clean): test_v6_assurance_validator.py -> 21/21 PASS including S2 controls '[PASS] planted operator-limited-claim-dropped fails closed' (CLM-GAMMA mutated to operator/LIMITED/P2, blocking emptied -> validate_operator_channel raises with 'channel drop', test lines 293-305) and '[PASS] derived known_limits entry satisfies the channel law' (claim-field naming passes, lines 306-316) — the planted drop is literally the CLM-DESCRIPTION-BUDGET defect shape from the kimi finding; test_v6_candidate_packet.py -> exit 0 'v6 candidate packet self-test: ok', whose S2 section (:171-182) builds a real packet via build_promotion_packet and asserts every operator-owned LIMITED P1/P2 class claim has a derived known_limits entry naming it and that CLM-DESCRIPTION-BUDGET specifically is channel-derived (S2 exemplar); plus '[PASS] planted hand-edited-blocking fails closed' (R12 drift) and the UNDISPOSITIONED_TRACKER_ITEMS generation refusal (P3 census fail-closed leg). Full validator on the pristine clone: exit 0 ('v6 assurance artifacts: schema + rule checks passed (ZI-001 + candidate)') — validate_operator_channel passes on the real artifacts. (v) SCHEMA: promotion-packet.schema.json known_limits items carry additionalProperties:false with a new optional 'claim' property (:121-125, description tying it to S2, pattern ^CLM-[A-Z0-9-]+$) and 'operator-hold' in the kind enum; the addition is load-bearing (without it the derived entry would violate additionalProperties:false) and new relative to the kimi subject SHA (diff 6db8c50..16b80ac: +5 lines; grep of all four S2 files at 6db8c50 for operator_channel/operator_limited_limits/claim = 0 hits each). All 10 known_limits entries and the packet top level conform to the schema's constraints (manual constraint validation — allowed keys, required keys, kind enum, claim pattern; python jsonschema not installed in this environment; note the schema is documentation/inventory-sealed — no repo script mechanically validates the packet against this schema file; the operative enforcement is the validator's hand-rolled checks plus validate_operator_channel). QUALIFICATION NOTE (does not defeat MET): neither (a) nor (b) alone literally describes the repair — (a)'s 'regardless of status' is not met in the packet channels (4 PROVED + 2 P3-census claims appear in neither blocking_claims nor known_limits) and (b)'s 'exempts' is not what the ruling does (it mandates the channel). But every claim outside a packet channel is expressly covered by the recorded ruling's PROVED/P3 limbs, the amendment lives in the register with the derivation agreeing, and the falsifier's governing threshold ('the ruling artifact exists and the amended criterion text matches the derivation'; 'Any unlisted operator-owned claim with no ruling leaves the defect standing') is satisfied on its letter — no unlisted operator-owned claim lacks a ruling. S2 retires by ruling-plus-code exactly as CL-2's dissent-preservation clause and Next-action item 2 contemplated.

new_findings.basin: Latent law gap: an operator-owned P3 claim that is NOT a tracker census row would occupy no machine channel and no census row without tripping any check — operator_channel_law limb 3 covers only 'P3 tracker census rows', and validate_operator_channel skips ALL P3 claims unconditionally (validate_v6_assurance.py:354-355 'if claim.get("consequence_severity", "P3") == "P3": continue'). No such claim exists at C+1 (both P3 operator claims are CLM-ISSUE-* census rows with reconciliation rows), and the ledger entry's revisit_when ('A claim class emerges that is operator-owned and open but fits neither blocking_claims nor a derivable known_limits entry') partially anticipates the class.

new_findings.basin: A matrix with consequence_severity absent on ALL claims degrades BOTH channel enforcements to notices instead of failures: validate_blocking_derivation returns ['LEGACY matrix without consequence_severity: blocking derivation not checked'] (validate_v6_assurance.py:321-322) and validate_operator_channel returns ['LEGACY matrix without consequence_severity: operator channel law not checked'] (:347-348) — notices do not fail the run. Effectively unreachable for a committed candidate: validate_matrix fails closed on PARTIAL severity ('all or none', :122-124, planted control '[PASS] planted partial-severity-matrix fails closed'), the digest inventory seals the committed matrix (any edit -> R5 DIGEST MISMATCH), the generator always emits severities, and test_v6_candidate_packet.py:55-57 asserts severity on every class claim. Residual exposure is only a from-scratch severity-less @2 freeze, which the C/C+1 regeneration discipline does not produce.

new_findings.basin: Two different owner tests coexist: derive_blocking uses set membership OPERATOR_CLASS_OWNERS = {operator, operator+agent, joint, independent-panel} (validate_v6_assurance.py:45,70) while the law text and validate_operator_channel use substring '"operator" in claim["owner"]' (:352). A future owner string containing 'operator' but outside the set (e.g. 'operator+ci') with non-PROVED non-LIMITED P1/P2 status would be omitted by derive_blocking yet required by validate_operator_channel -> the generator would emit a packet its own validator rejects. Fail-CLOSED polarity (loud, no silent drop), so a generation-time confusion seam only; every owner string at C+1 containing 'operator' (operator, operator+agent) is in the set.
